objective: Derive a girth-dependent induced-shore size criterion and precisely exclude its fixed-degree arbitrary-girth extrapolation, preserving the finite C11 witness and the original quantifier.

atomic_claims.text: Explicit vertex-rooted and edge-rooted counts give n>=M(k,g) for minimum degree k; an MC in an r-regular graph requires at least 2M(r-1,g) vertices.
For every integer g>=7, M(4,g)>=2M(3,g), so no degree-four graph can satisfy the strict size-only no-MC criterion there.
At each fixed regular degree r>=3, the graph's own necessary size eventually exceeds the two-shore threshold; an explicit sufficient cutoff is given.
At fixed d only finitely many integer regular degrees r<d qualify, so growing r cannot rescue this size-only unbounded-girth proposal; other no-MC methods are not excluded.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs, girth at least g, actual minimum-degree or regular-degree hypotheses, and two nonempty MC shores.
The attempted unbounded-girth subdirection is explicitly restricted to n>=2; K1 remains in the frozen root.
The displayed finite-sum and recurrence arguments use no T3, TABC, T14 or graph-existence theorem.
risks: Failure of this sufficient criterion does not imply MC existence.
No graph generator, solver or mathematical verifier ran; both obligations remain open.
